headline: PLS.AX takes a 4.7% hit as lithium gloom lingers, GTA VI pre-orders confirmed for June 25th giving TTWO a boost last night, and the RBA holds rates steady — giving mortgage holders a welcome breather.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dropped sharply today, closing at $5.88. Lithium prices remain under pressure with no clear recovery catalyst in sight — China's lithium market is still oversupplied, keeping a lid on what miners like PLS can earn for their product. It's been a rough run and today's session continued that trend.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets slipped today, down 0.74% to $94.44. This fund tracks developing economies like China, India and Brazil, and broad risk-off sentiment on the ASX weighed on it. The Aussie dollar softening slightly didn't provide much of a buffer either.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Global energy companies edged lower today, closing at $8.10. Oil prices are essentially flat around US$76.58 a barrel, but a ceasefire agreement in the Middle East earlier this week took some of the fear premium out of oil — that's less tailwind for energy stocks.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped 0.56% to $76.83 today, dragged down by a broad ASX sell-off that saw the ASX 200 fall 1.53%. As a diversified fund with heavy Australian and global equities exposure, it tends to move with the wider market.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: A small green day for the AI ETF, up 0.22% to $18.16. AI-related stocks continue to attract interest globally, and while the gain is modest, it's a positive signal that the theme is holding up even on a tough day for the broader ASX.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS was almost flat today, nudging up 0.07% to $525.46. This ETF tracks the entire US sharemarket and it's the one holding that managed to stay in the green today — reflecting the strength of last night's US session feeding through to the ASX-listed price.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: No fresh price data for tonight — US markets haven't opened yet. Last night's close was US$362.10. Recent news is positive though: Alphabet reportedly beat earnings by 94% and doubled its cloud backlog to $460 billion. Analysts are watching AI progress and Waymo risks closely.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft's last known close was US$378.91, with US markets yet to open tonight. No fresh news today — the stock has been steady, and the broader AI tailwind continues to support Microsoft's cloud and Azure business.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Big news last night: Rockstar Games confirmed GTA VI pre-orders begin June 25. Take-Two stock rose on the announcement — this is the most anticipated game release in years and pre-order numbers will be closely watched as a signal of just how big the launch could be.

watch_today.title: GTA VI pre-orders open June 25 — TTWO catalyst incoming
watch_today.detail: Rockstar Games confirmed yesterday that GTA VI pre-orders kick off on June 25 — that's less than a week away. This is a monster moment for Take-Two (TTWO), which you hold. Pre-order volumes will be the first hard data point on how big this launch actually is. US markets open tonight, so watch for TTWO to pop. Hold your position — the thesis is playing out.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX down 4.7% today — lithium pain continues
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals shed 4.7% today to close at $5.88, and you're now sitting on a 12.76% loss on this position. Lithium prices remain weak due to an oversupplied market in China, and there's no clear near-term recovery catalyst. Unless you believe in a medium-term lithium rebound, this is worth a serious look. No strong buy signal here right now.

watch_today.title: GOOG: cloud backlog doubled to $460B — strong fundamental case
watch_today.detail: A 24/7 Wall St. piece out yesterday highlighted that Alphabet beat earnings by 94% and doubled its Google Cloud backlog to $460 billion. That's a massive forward revenue signal. With GOOG last closing at US$362.10 and US markets opening tonight, this is a stock with real momentum. Your position is small — worth keeping an eye on whether to add.

watch_today.title: RBA holds interest rates — mortgage holders get a breather
watch_today.detail: The RBA left rates on hold today, giving millions of Aussie homeowners relief from further repayment increases. Some economists (per the AFR) still think more hikes are coming, so this isn't necessarily the all-clear. For your portfolio, a rate hold is broadly positive — it keeps consumer spending supported and reduces pressure on growth stocks.

watch_today.title: ASX 200 down 1.53% today — broad sell-off hits most of your holdings
watch_today.detail: The ASX dropped 137 points today to 8,828 — a significant down day. Most of your ASX holdings fell in line with the market. VTS.AX and GXAI.AX were the only two to stay in the green. Nothing specific triggered the sell-off in your holdings — it was broad market weakness rather than stock-specific news.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX nudging up despite ASX sell-off — AI theme holding firm
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF (GXAI.AX) was up 0.22% today even as the broader ASX fell 1.53%. That's a small but meaningful sign of relative strength. The AI investment theme continues to attract money globally, and with Alphabet's cloud backlog news providing a positive backdrop, this one looks steady.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a rough Friday, falling 1.53% to close at 8,828 — one of the bigger single-day drops in recent weeks. Gold pulled back 1.25% to US$4,171 after a strong run, which suggests some investors are feeling a touch more confident and moving out of safe-haven assets. Oil is virtually unchanged at US$76.58 a barrel. The Aussie dollar is steady at around 70.1 US cents. US markets (S&P 500 last at 7,420; NASDAQ at 26,021) haven't opened yet tonight — they'll be the next big signal, especially with the GTA VI pre-order story giving gaming stocks a reason to move.

indicators.note: Broad sell-off on the ASX today — most sectors fell.

indicators.note: Last night's close. US markets open tonight ~11:30 PM AEST.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night's close. Tech-heavy index — watch for TTWO and GOOG moves tonight.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Essentially flat. Middle East ceasefire took some heat out of the oil price earlier this week.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold pulled back today — still elevated but some profit-taking after a big run.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar barely moved — hovering just above 70 US cents.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is the RBA holding interest rates steady, giving mortgage holders some relief. Meanwhile, Albanese's government is navigating a messy political battle over capital gains tax (CGT) changes — announcing carve-outs for small businesses after a budget backlash, while the Greens are holding up NDIS reforms. It's a busy week in Canberra.

stories.title: RBA holds interest rates on hold — relief for borrowers
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank left interest rates unchanged today, meaning no more pain at the mortgage repayment level — for now. However, some economists quoted in the AFR reckon more hikes are still on the table if inflation doesn't keep cooling. For property owners and borrowers, this is a short-term win, but it's not necessarily the end of the rate cycle.

stories.title: Albanese announces CGT exemptions for small businesses after budget backlash
stories.why_it_matters: After a backlash from small business owners over the budget's proposed changes to capital gains tax (CGT — the tax you pay when you sell an asset for a profit), Prime Minister Albanese has announced 'generous' exemptions specifically for small businesses. Treasurer Chalmers also moved to wind back ministerial powers in the CGT legislation to help clear a Senate hurdle. The government is trying to pass broader CGT reforms — including reducing the 50% CGT discount for investors — but is clearly feeling political heat.

stories.title: NDIS reforms face delay as Greens play hardball
stories.why_it_matters: The Greens are holding up the government's NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme) reform legislation in the Senate, using their numbers as leverage in broader budget negotiations. This is a significant delay for a scheme that supports hundreds of thousands of Australians with disabilities. The standoff reflects the broader tension between the Albanese government and the Greens over budget priorities.

stories.title: Banks watching RBA pause closely — what it means for CBA, NAB and ANZ
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's big banks are watching the RBA's decision carefully because interest rate levels directly affect their net interest margins — the gap between what they charge on loans versus what they pay on deposits. A rate hold means margins stay roughly where they are. CBA, NAB and ANZ have all been benefiting from higher rates over the past few years, so any eventual cuts will squeeze their profits. Today's hold buys them more time at current margin levels.

ai.summary: Today's AI news is dominated by regulation chatter — the UK, EU, and US are all wrestling with how to oversee AI without strangling innovation. There's also a cracking deal spotted for AI tool subscriptions that power users might want to know about.

stories.title: Britain betting it can regulate AI without a catastrophe
stories.why_it_matters: The UK is taking a deliberately light-touch approach to regulating AI — rather than writing new laws, it's relying on existing regulators in each sector (finance, health, etc.) to manage AI risks. The bet is that flexibility beats rigidity when the technology is moving so fast. This matters for AI investors because lighter UK regulation could attract more AI investment and development there, benefiting global AI companies including Google (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT).

stories.title: AI regulation should be rational, not retaliatory — EFF pushes back on US proposals
stories.why_it_matters: The Electronic Frontier Foundation (a major US digital rights group) is warning that some proposed US AI regulations are being driven by political rivalry with China rather than genuine safety concerns. They argue rules designed to 'punish' foreign AI could end up harming domestic innovation too. For investors in US AI names like GOOG and MSFT, the shape of US regulation is a key risk to watch over the next 12 months.

stories.title: EU AI Act: What it means for energy use and sustainability
stories.why_it_matters: The EU's AI Act — the world's most comprehensive AI rulebook — includes requirements around environmental impact and energy consumption of AI systems. As data centres powering large AI models consume enormous amounts of electricity, this is becoming a real cost and compliance issue for big tech companies. It's an emerging risk for AI ETFs like GXAI.AX if energy costs or compliance burdens bite into margins.

stories.title: ChatGPT Plus is $240/year — but you can get 5 years of ChatGPT, Claude & Gemini for $99.99
stories.why_it_matters: A deal spotted by Boing Boing offers 5 years of access to ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini — the three biggest AI assistant tools — for just US$99.99, compared to ChatGPT Plus alone costing US$240/year. If you're using any of these tools for research, writing or work, this is a significant saving. It also signals that AI tool pricing is getting competitive, which is good for consumers but squeezes margins for the companies behind the models.

sport.summary: NRL Round 16 kicks off tonight with Knights v Dragons at 8pm. There's key late mail to know before you lock in your tips — Kalyn Ponga is out, which is a big blow for the Knights. The AFL also has some news worth noting.

stories.title: Round 16 Late Mail: Ponga ruled out, Katoa also out, Brailey in the mix
stories.why_it_matters: Key late mail for Round 16: Kalyn Ponga (Knights) has been ruled out, which is a massive blow to Newcastle heading into tonight's game against the Dragons. Edrick Lee Katoa is also out. Robbie Brailey is in the mix to return, which could help the Knights at dummy half. If you're tipping tonight, Newcastle just got a lot harder to back without their star fullback.

stories.why_it_matters: Expert tips are out for all Round 16 matches. With Ponga missing for the Knights tonight, the Dragons may be a sneaky tip. The Titans host the Panthers on Saturday at Cbus Super Stadium on the Gold Coast — the home ground advantage could be interesting but Penrith remain the benchmark. Check the full article for match-by-match breakdowns.

stories.title: DCE reality check and Bulldogs' 'real problem' laid bare
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports has published a deep-dive calling out the Bulldogs' structural problems ahead of their Saturday night clash with the Sea Eagles at Accor Stadium. The piece also questions whether Dally M medallist DCE (Daly Cherry-Evans) — on a reported $600k contract — is still delivering at the level that justifies his price tag. The Dogs are said to be 'shellshocked' and their issues run deeper than just results on the scoreboard.

stories.why_it_matters: The NRL signings tracker has been updated: Brisbane Broncos star Ken Arthars is joining Catalans Dragons in a notable move, while Fa'amanu Brown (Faulalo) and Josh Luke have both extended their current contracts. Player movement news worth tracking as clubs lock in their 2027 rosters.
